args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy deploy v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 18% while running v2.3.1.

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout to all three regions.

Current status: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0, service reports healthy, error rate 0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1 was never healthy in production. Any future attempt to redeploy v2.3.1 requires change-manager approval. Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined and needs investigation.

trace.final:
The incident did go through (INC-0001, open) — no retry needed.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was running v2.3.1 in all three production regions with failing health checks and an 18% error rate. Release history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent production-healthy release (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a valid target).

**Rollback:** The first rollback attempt to v2.3.0 failed partially — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west were still on the unhealthy v2.3.1. A retry completed the rollout.

**Verified result:** All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001 opened at SEV2, documenting the failure, the partial-rollback-then-retry sequence, and current healthy state.

Two things worth flagging:
- The initial rollback call reported an error but had already changed us-east. A blind retry was the right move here, but that error mode means "rollback failed" doesn't reliably mean "nothing changed" — worth verifying region state after any partial failure.
- v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it would require change-manager approval. Root cause of the health check failures is still unknown and is the real outstanding work behind this incident.
